Based on my search, I can provide you with comprehensive information about the **Navy P-3 Orion**, the legendary maritime patrol aircraft.

## Overview

The **P-3 Orion** is a four-engine turboprop anti-submarine and maritime surveillance aircraft developed by Lockheed for the United States Navy in the 1960s. It was based on the L-188 Electra commercial airliner and is easily distinguished by its distinctive tail stinger or "MAD" boom used for magnetic anomaly detection of submarines.

## Specifications (P-3C Orion)

| Parameter | Specification |
|-----------|---------------|
| **Mission** | Anti-submarine warfare (ASW), anti-surface warfare (ASuW), and surveillance |
| **Crew** | 11 (including pilots and sensor operators) |
| **Length** | 116.7 ft (35.57 m) |
| **Wingspan** | 99.6 ft (30.38 m) |
| **Height** | 33.7 ft (10.27 m) |
| **Maximum Gross Takeoff Weight** | 139,760 lb (63,394 kg) |
| **Propulsion** | Four Allison T-56-A-14 turboprop engines (4,600 hp each) |
| **Fuel Capacity** | 9,200 US gallons |

## Armament Capabilities

The P-3 can carry a wide variety of weapons:
- **Missiles**: AGM-84 Harpoon, AGM-84E SLAM, AGM-84H/K SLAM-ER, AGM-65 Maverick
- **Torpedoes**: Mk-46, Mk-50, Mk-54
- **Other**: Rockets, mines, depth bombs, and various gravity bombs

These can be carried internally in the bomb bay under the front fuselage and on underwing pylons.

## Key Features

- **Magnetic Anomaly Detection (MAD)**: Located in the extended fiberglass tail stinger, capable of detecting submarines by sensing magnetic anomalies in Earth's magnetic field
- **Internal bomb bay**: Houses torpedoes and special weapons
- **Underwing stations**: Additional pylons for various armament configurations

## Operational History

The P-3 Orion has seen extensive service including:
- **Vietnam War**: Operation Market Time coastal patrols (1964 onwards)
- **Gulf War (1990-1991)**: Maritime surveillance, identification, and targeting support
- **Hainan Island Incident (2001)**: EP-3E variant involved in collision with Chinese J-8II interceptor

## Current Status (2025)

The P-3 Orion is being phased out of U.S. Navy service in favor of the **P-8 Poseidon**, but remains active with numerous international operators:

- **United States**: Only **6 active P-3 Orions** remain in U.S. Navy service as of October 2025 (with VX-30 and VXS-1 squadrons)
- **Japan**: Gradually replacing P-3Cs with domestically produced **Kawasaki P-1** aircraft; preparing to transfer some P-3Cs to the Philippines by 2027
- **Germany**: Completed P-3 retirement in late 2025, transitioning to **P-8A Poseidon**
- **Greece**: After more than a decade of delays, the first upgraded **P-3B Orion** completed its maiden flight on September 2, 2025
- **Portugal**: Operating P-3C CUP+ aircraft; received ex-German Navy P-3Cs
- **Canada**: Operating **CP-140 Aurora** (Canadian variant of P-3)
- **Argentina**: Receiving second-hand P-3C aircraft (second aircraft delivered October 2025)
- **NOAA**: Continues to operate **WP-3D Orion** aircraft for hurricane hunting and atmospheric research

## Variants

- **P-3C**: Main production version
- **EP-3**: ELINT (Electronic Intelligence) variant
- **OP-3C**: Reconnaissance variant
- **UP-3C/D**: Equipment testing and training variants
- **CP-140 Aurora**: Canadian variant with different avionics
- **WP-3D**: NOAA weather research variant

The P-3 Orion remains one of the most successful and long-serving maritime patrol aircraft in aviation history, with over 757 built and service spanning more than six decades.

Sources:
1. https://www.vp4association.com/aircraft-information-2/32-2/
2. https://www.seaforces.org/marint/Japan-Maritime-Self-Defense-Force/AIRCRAFT/Kawasaki-P-3-MPA.htm
3. https://www.p3orion.nl/news.html
4. https://airbornescience.nasa.gov/sites/default/files/P-3B%20Experimenter%20Handbook%20548-HDBK-0001.pdf
5. https://www.navalnews.com/naval-news/2025/09/upgraded-hellenic-navy-p-3b-orion-completes-first-flight/
